notes.title: The epic dungeon crawler gets a huge update!
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/7a71ed5a7cf34c861db211c81c0808bf9a2cbfed.jpg

Evil is on the move again. After centuries of bloodshed and war, the last heroes fell to the growing tide of monstrosities, their memory fading away like sand in a gale. The land of Talon Coast is helpless, as the armies of darkness surge forward, threatening to extinguish the very light of the sun. But there is one last bastion of hope, one final attempt at abating the flood of corruption: Claudius, High Priest of the Temple of Heavenshine, sacrifices the holiest relic of the land to summon the fallen heroes back to life! Weakened by their own resurrection, yet determined to return hope and justice to the land of Talon, the reborn heroes will wage war against this scheming evil in its many hideous forms.

[previewyoutube=0JeYOs7gHHI;full][/previewyoutube]
2-5 players
60-90 minutes
Dungeon crawling, cooperative, epic adventure!

In Sword & Sorcery, one to five players control heroes with unique powers. The heroes will fight together against the forces of evil - controlled by the game system itself - to save the kingdom and break the spell that binds their souls. They will explore dangerous ruins, ominous forests, and besieged cities. Their skills and abilities are the last, best hope of Talon’s Coast.

[previewyoutube=t5n4MNk7XhU;full][/previewyoutube]
Sword & Sorcery's game system represents the perfect evolution of the mechanics first used in Galaxy Defenders. From its forerunner, Sword & Sorcery inherits key features such as advanced AI for monsters, a high degree of character customization, and multiple tactical options during battles. At the same time, gameplay in Sword & Sorcery is fast and dynamic, thanks to an innovative area movement and area control system, and includes new features never seen before in a game of this category.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/2e98096c12e9fd727f719332dd1bed38aa718159.jpg

The Tabletopia version of the game has received a MAJOR update, with the entire of Immortal Souls (Act 1 of 3) now available to play (2-3 players 100% free, 4-5 players with a Premium subscription)!

Play it now on Tabletopia!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/eb19920c1019fd717a98d8f75bdad62c1a976236.jpg

notes.title: Hunt, fish, and gather in this Stone Age version of the tile-laying classic.
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/1ad43440a1eb61b1ddbce183f1ea0a1eb9d0ad83.jpg

Carcassonne: Hunters and Gatherers is a standalone game in the Carcassonne series set in the stone age.

As in other Carcassonne games, players take turns placing tiles to create the landscape and placing meeples to score points from the map they're creating. The player with the most points at the end of the game wins.

[previewyoutube=9dml4XeACyU;full][/previewyoutube]
Instead of cities, roads, and farms, Carcassonne: Hunters and Gatherers has forests, rivers, lakes, and meadows. Players' meeples can represent hunters (when placed in the meadows), gatherers (in a forest), or fishermen (on a river segment). They also have huts, which can be placed on rivers or lakes to get fish from the entire river system.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/e42947da1b0483584dffd9eb8ff0931be2fae412.jpg

It includes many of the familiar mechanics from Carcassonne with a few new rules, including:
- A player who completes a forest with a gold nugget in it gets to immediately draw and place 1 of 12 bonus (menhir) tiles.
- A meadow is worth 2 points for every animal in it, except tigers, which negate certain other animals.
- A river segment is worth the number of tiles in the segment plus the number of fish in the lakes at each end.
- A fishing hut scores at the end of the game and is worth the number of fish in all the lakes connected by rivers.

Play it now on Tabletopia!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11995444/09af555ea89db9f6da081dda7f84589be514a5d6.jpg

notes.title: Tabletopia Update: March 17
notes.notes:
In this recent update we introduce a special Solo mode that let's you start solitaire games faster and easier.

For games that support one-player mode, you can now select solo or multiplayer mode directly on the game's page. If you click Play Solo, the appropriate setup will start launching immediately. 

Chat, turn-based modes, and lobby are disabled for this mode.

http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11995444/b7a6b7913333ec0093fec400b2a410490c26be95.png

Other Features
Optimized execution time for most frequent actions, such as Join/Leave Seat, Start/Pause Game, etc. 

Bugs Fixed
IE/Edge: header caching errors.
IE: stars were not displayed on bookmarked games.
Mac-Steam All Games: category drop-down was not correctly displayed. 
Tokens with enabled Complex Collider could not be put into bags.

notes.title: Tabletopia Update: March 2
notes.notes:
Hey Tabletopians,

New update just rolled out and with it we introduce new Game Categories in our catalog. Categories were created to make browsing for games on the portal even more convenient. Now you can quickly find solo, two-player, classic, Top BGG and other games.

http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11995444/e3761afb786afedb5558ebdf78e960cb381dde16.png

With this update we have also added improved pre-game messages displayed while the game is loading. Now you will see there a lot of useful tips and advice for players and designers alike. We hope you find them helpful!

Bugs fixed:
 Game pages: Custom links (BGG pages, Kickstarter campaigns, etc.)  were not displayed. 
Lobby: After sending an invite players could send another invitation by clicking the area were the Invite button was.
 Various stability improvements and minor fixes.

notes.title: Tabletopia Update: February 15
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, a new update on Tabletopia just rolled out!

Features
Game: When players place dice into bags, their upper side is now kept. Also, when drawing dice from a bag at the start of a game, they now appear randomized, which is important while playing such games as Roll Player
Various improvements on the portal.

Fixed
Sometimes rooms failed to be displayed in Find & Play.
Errors while searching for games with apostrophe in their titles.

Happy gaming, see you at the table!

notes.title: Tabletopia Update: February 9
notes.notes:
Hey Tabletopians,

Here’s a list of features and fixes from our latest release.

Features
Game page: Improved access to rules, added list of setups.
Country and city selection in player profile made easier, and other minor improvements.
Lobby: You will now be asked to confirm that you want to leave the lobby if you already took a seat.
Game: Added Korea and India regions to game servers to reduce ping, improve response and stability for players from these regions.
Game: You can now use magnetic map for decks.

Fixed:
Player profile: City selection for certain countries.
Game: While moving or rotating an object other objects on top of it did not keep their position.
Find & Play: Players directly took seats in the lobby by clicking “Open Lobby” in the Details pop-up.
Find & Play: Players could not create new rooms due to erroneous room limits.
Find & Play: Players received notification "Room not found" after clicking the room ID in the general chat.

Happy gaming, and see you at the table!

notes.title: Keyflower Tournament Update: Registration closed, matches schedule under way
notes.notes:
Hey Tabletopians,

On February, 1 player registration for the first International Online Keyflower Tournament was closed. 64 people from over 20 countries signed up to take part and compete to win our prizes! 

 
http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11995444/60c1dabd402c26cd5226f4a090cb1354dbc50282.png

Tournament Schedule
During the next week the tournament schedule will be formed and made available. We're striving to make all matches convenient for participants from the various countries.

The games will start not earlier than February, 10, and some participants will have their matches later. Each contestant will be contacted on email to let them know the date and time of their games. 
 
Discord and Training Matches
In the meantime, you can join the tournament channel on Discord, where you can contact other players and schedule training games. Free training room is available on Tabletopia.

We're also planning on streaming some of the tournament matches. Stay tuned!

notes.title: Tabletopia Update: December 21
notes.notes:
Hey Tabletopians, 

A couple of useful features were added in our recent update which make playing Tabletopia on Steam more comfortable:
In-game Steam-overlay enabled. It allows you to access Steam whilst in-game, send messages to friends, invite friends, etc.
Screenshots capturing through Steam added. Now you can save game screenshots in Tabletopia just like in any other Steam game!
Enjoy, and see you at the table!

notes.title: Tabletopia Stability & Performance Update: December 7
notes.notes:
Greetings,

Thank you everyone for your feedback and reviews during release. In the latest update we mostly focused on stability and performance of the game.

FIXED

 Crashes and freezes on Windows 10 when 'Alt' key is pressed.
 Connection issues on start while application loading.
 Heavy CPU load.
 Laptop & Macbook battery drains fast and works very noisily.
 Loading some pages takes up to several minutes.


Overall performance and stability improvements.

notes.title: Tabletopia Tech Update: November 10
notes.notes:
Hi Tabletopians,

The latest technical update brings a few fixes to Tabletopia.

Features:
Users who registered through Steam or their social network accounts can now create Tabletopia login/password in their profile.

Bugs Fixed:
Synchronization errors in game client. Due to unstable connection the board and other game components were sometimes displayed differently to different players during the game.
After activating an invite code and logging in through social media, demo users needed to re-login to access Workshop. Otherwise it was not accessible.
Wrong password alert was not displayed in the login form in Firefox.
Performance and overall improvements.

notes.title: Tabletopia Update - April 8th, 2016
notes.notes:
Hi all,

With the latest Tabletopia update, we’ve included the Windows 32-bit version of the Tabletopia Steam client. We have also included DirectX v.11 and some other packages to be installed if required.

Specific changes include:

Improvements

     Friends: Added ability to search players by name or login
     Friends: Ability to add player to your friends list from that player’s profile
     Find&Play: Find&Play automatically refreshes (showing newly created rooms immediately)
Find&Play: Your own private rooms are excluded from the list
 
Fixes

     Fixed: Duplicated accounts displayed in ‘Friends’ when friend has 2+ connected logins (e.g. Steam, Facebook, Google)
     Fixed: For some players, 'Get Activation Code’ was displayed on login to Tabletopia Web portal
